targetWork.author: Michael A. Jalandoon
targetWork.title: Heavy metals and physicochemical assessment of water, sediments and Oreochromis niloticus (Tilapia) in Maragondon River, Philippines

method: Reviewed official AEA-IRC/DLSU-D library and access-policy pages and targeted public web-index searches. The institution routes users to its OPAC, but a record-specific catalog search was not completed and no thesis text was accessed. A subsequent unauthenticated attempt to open the OPAC basic-search entry redirected to the generic site-selection welcome page; no catalog form or record-level results were returned, and no login or request was submitted. The 2024 Maragondon River article independently cites the 2018 thesis bibliographically, but this does not establish public catalog access or thesis-text availability.

institutionalSources.finding: DLSU-D AEA-IRC describes its Archives and Special Collection as maintaining the DLSU-D Access to Institutional Repository for digitized theses, dissertations and university publications.

The current online-services FAQ says A.I.R. is temporarily suspended due to technical issues, points users to the OPAC, and states full-text thesis access requires proof of author permission; requests may be for a full text or author-approved pages.
Official DLSU-D library contact and service page.

searchOutcome.reason: The institutional route identifies the catalog and collection, but the unauthenticated OPAC entry point redirected before exposing its search form. The thesis is cited in a 2024 article, which confirms a bibliographic lead only; repository suspension and author-authorization requirements remain access limits, not evidence that the thesis or its claims are absent.

catalogAttempt.result: Redirected to the generic DLSU-D site-selection welcome page; no title/author query was submitted and no record-level result was retrieved.
catalogAttempt.citationLead: The 2024 Limbago et al. Maragondon River article cites Jalandoon (2018) as a DLSU-D Masters Thesis.

decision.reason: The institutional access policy does not expose the target thesis content or authorize redistribution. Keep the Oreochromis niloticus specimen claim held until the thesis protocol/voucher evidence and item-specific reuse permission can be checked.

nextAction: If the species-level thesis claim remains important, ask DLSU-D AEA-IRC whether it can confirm the catalog metadata/abstract and what author permission is required for a full-text review. Do not send a request without explicit authorization; do not reuse thesis-derived material without permission.
